logline: A nervous caretaker, tormented by an old man’s filmed pale-blue eye, murders him after midnight vigils, conceals the body beneath the floorboards, then confesses when he believes police can hear the dead heart still beating.

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Narrator insists he is nervous but not mad; hearing is over-acute.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: True!—nervous—very, very dreadfully nervous I had been and am; but why will you say that I am mad?

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Motive forms around the old man’s vulture-like pale blue filmed eye; narrator loves the man but resolves to kill him to be rid of the eye.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: I think it was his eye! yes, it was this! He had the eye of a vulture—a pale blue eye, with a film over it.

source_grounded_timeline.summary: For seven nights at midnight narrator opens the door, thrusts in a dark lantern, and seeks the open eye; each morning he is kindly.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: And this I did for seven long nights—every night just at midnight—but I found the eye always closed

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Eighth night: door opened with extreme caution; old man startles; narrator freezes an hour after “Who’s there?”
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: my thumb slipped upon the tin fastening, and the old man sprang up in bed, crying out—“Who’s there?”

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Lantern ray hits the open Evil Eye; narrator hears the old man’s heart like a watch in cotton; leaps, kills him under the bed.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: In an instant I dragged him to the floor, and pulled the heavy bed over him.

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Body dismembered; parts hidden under three floor planks; tub catches blood; no stains.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: I then took up three planks from the flooring of the chamber, and deposited all between the scantlings.

source_grounded_timeline.summary: At four o’clock police arrive after a neighbour heard a shriek; narrator tours them and sits above the corpse.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: there came a knocking at the street door... three men, who introduced themselves... as officers of the police.

source_grounded_timeline.summary: Imagined heartbeat grows; narrator raves and confesses, demanding the planks be torn up.
source_grounded_timeline.source_evidence: “Villains!” I shrieked, “dissemble no more! I admit the deed!—tear up the planks!—here, here!—It is the beating of his hideous heart!”

withheld_name_rules.policy: Source withholds personal names for narrator and old man; keep them unnamed on screen and in credits of character.
rules: Do not assign a proper given name to the narrator or the old man.
Police may be addressed only as officers; no invented individual names.
Neighbour remains offscreen/unseen unless strictly required as sound motivation.
withheld_name_rules.source_evidence: calling him by name in a hearty tone

essential_beats.description: Opening claim of sanity and acute hearing.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Above all was the sense of hearing acute.

essential_beats.description: The eye identified as sole motive.
essential_beats.source_evidence: Whenever it fell upon me, my blood ran cold

essential_beats.description: Seven midnight lantern vigils; eye closed.
essential_beats.source_evidence: I put in a dark lantern, all closed, closed, that no light shone out

essential_beats.description: Eighth night discovery, heart-sound, murder under bed.
essential_beats.source_evidence: a low, dull, quick sound, such as a watch makes when enveloped in cotton.
First of all I dismembered the corpse. I cut off the head and the arms and the legs.

essential_beats.description: Police search; narrator sits on burial spot; auditory breakdown and confession.
essential_beats.source_evidence: placed my own seat upon the very spot beneath which reposed the corpse of the victim.

scene_outline.heading: INT. HOUSE - NIGHT
scene_outline.purpose: Establish narrator’s address to an unseen listener and dread of madness accusation.
scene_outline.source_evidence: how healthily—how calmly I can tell you the whole story.

scene_outline.heading: INT. OLD MAN'S CHAMBER - DAY/NIGHT MONTAGE
scene_outline.purpose: Show kindness by day and seven cautious midnight inspections with lantern ray.
scene_outline.source_evidence: I was never kinder to the old man than during the whole week before I killed him.

scene_outline.heading: INT. OLD MAN'S CHAMBER - NIGHT (EIGHTH)
scene_outline.purpose: Eighth entry, startle, hour of stillness, open eye, heartbeat, killing.
scene_outline.source_evidence: Upon the eighth night I was more than usually cautious in opening the door.

scene_outline.heading: INT. OLD MAN'S CHAMBER - NIGHT (AFTER)
scene_outline.purpose: Concealment under planks; tub; four o’clock.
scene_outline.source_evidence: When I had made an end of these labors, it was four o’clock—still dark as midnight.

scene_outline.heading: INT. HOUSE STREET DOOR / CHAMBER - PREDAWN
scene_outline.purpose: Police arrival, tour, seated chat over corpse, rising pulse-sound, confession.
scene_outline.source_evidence: A shriek had been heard by a neighbour during the night; suspicion of foul play had been aroused
